findings.message: the solver derived the output "[]\n4821"; the code prints "['owner']\n4821"
findings.resolution: Not a defect: the code prints ['owner'] and 4821 because Object.keys lists the string key owner and skips only the symbol key, so the solver's [] was a misreading and the item states it correctly.

findings.message: Hint 3 ('Start with start, add deposit, then take away fee') spells out the whole expression in order, so the learner no longer has to build it; it should only point at the rule (each step uses the previous result).
findings.resolution: Fixed: hint 3 of reassignment write-01 now names the rule (replace the variable in the second step by the whole first step) instead of spelling out the order of operations.

findings.message: Hint 2 names the operator (||) and its rule, and hint 3 then gives the operand order ('username on the left and guest on the right'). Together they spell out the whole expression, so nothing is left for the learner to write.
findings.resolution: Fixed: hint 2 no longer names the operator and hint 3 now asks the learner to test the expression with '' and 'Mo' instead of giving the operand order.

findings.message: The feedback for 8 says 'You ran the else block as well'. If both blocks ran, fee would still be 2 right after line 4 (the else assignment is on line 6, after the probe). The value 8 only follows from taking the else block instead of the if block, so the named belief does not produce this option at the asked moment.
findings.resolution: Fixed: the feedback for 8 now says it comes from taking the else block as if the condition were false, and the option is retagged condition-direction-flipped.

findings.message: The feedback for option '6\nshipped' says the learner thought the 6 is shown as soon as return runs, with line 3 running afterwards. The 6 is printed by the console.log on line 5, which can only run after ship has finished, so the named belief (lines after return still run) actually produces 'shipped\n6' (the other option), not this one. The feedback gives a mechanism (return itself shows the value) that does not exist in the code and teaches a false model of when the value is printed.
findings.resolution: Fixed: the feedback for '6\nshipped' now describes the belief that really gives it (6 goes back to line 5 and line 3 still runs afterwards).

findings.message: The option '35' is tagged with the misconception one-based-index (counting starts at 1), but that belief does not produce 35: a learner who thinks index 1 is the first item would add the first and second laps (12 + 9). The feedback text itself explains 35 with a different cause (reading as if i started at 0), so the tag and the feedback disagree and the option is attributed to the wrong mistaken belief.
findings.resolution: Fixed: declared the misconception start-value-ignored (loop visits every item as if it began at index 0) and retagged option 35 to it, matching its feedback.

findings.message: Option '1 2' is tagged delete-keeps-key (delete only empties the value, the key stays). Worked through the code that belief makes kit.pc read as empty or undefined, not 1, so it does not give this option's value. Only the belief that delete does nothing at all gives 1 2, and the feedback names no belief. The feedback also adds 'reading pc gives nothing', which goes one step past the missing fact (delete removes the key) and tells the learner what the pc read prints.
findings.resolution: Fixed: the '1 2' option now carries a new declared misconception delete-does-nothing (the belief that delete changes nothing, which does print 1 2) and its feedback no longer says what the pc read prints.

findings.message: Option '3 1' encodes 'map combines results into one value'. Worked through, that belief makes bonus a single number, so bonus.length is undefined, not 1. The feedback does not match the value the option shows (the belief would give 'undefined 7').
findings.resolution: Fixed: the option '1 7' became 'undefined 7', the output the collapse-to-one-value belief really gives (checked by running it), and its feedback no longer implies bonus has a length.

findings.message: The prompt never states the label format. It only gives the example "crate-1", yet the function takes a prefix parameter and no "crate" appears in the signature. A learner has to guess that the label is prefix, a dash and the counter; the separator and the role of prefix are not stated.
findings.resolution: Fixed: the prompt now states that each label is the prefix, a dash and a private counter starting at 1, with the example prefix 'crate' giving crate-1 and crate-2.

findings.message: Hint 3 ('Check which line prints undefined and which one throws') tells the learner that one of the two reads prints undefined and the other throws. That is the whole outcome of the snippet and singles out the correct option, so the learner no longer has to work out the difference between a declared and an undeclared name.
findings.resolution: Fixed: hint 3 now asks the learner to compare how each of the two names is introduced before line 4 runs, without saying which read prints undefined and which throws.

findings.message: Hint 3 ('Add the first two changes and leave the handler's 100 out') spells out which terms make up the answer and which option terms to drop. It carries the calculation to its end and eliminates the 111 and 10 options, so the learner no longer has to decide which additions happen before line 10.
findings.resolution: Fixed: hint 3 of promise-basics trace-01 now asks whether line 8 can already have run when line 10 prints, without telling the learner which terms to add; the sibling '10' option was retagged to a new executor-runs-later misconception and the rest of the lesson's hint 3s were checked.

findings.message: Hint 3 ('Follow the path: button, then its li, then the ul. Read which id each listener prints.') spells out the full bubbling order of elements. Only reading three ids off the tree is left, so the hint hands over the printed sequence instead of narrowing the choice.
findings.resolution: Fixed: hint 3 of event-propagation predict-01 now points at lines 8 to 10 and what each listener prints instead of spelling out the button, li, ul path; the other hint 3s of the lesson that gave results away were reworded too.

findings.message: The feedback for 'packing\nparcel\nshipping' names the belief 'the then handler runs the moment it is attached'. In this code job.then is attached on line 6, after console.log('shipping') on line 5, so that belief gives packing, shipping, parcel, which is the correct answer. To get parcel before shipping, the learner must think the handler runs as soon as ok('parcel') fulfills the promise inside the executor. The named thought does not produce this option's value.
findings.resolution: Fixed: the 'packing, parcel, shipping' option now names a new resolve-delivers-at-once misconception (the value reaches the handler the moment ok is called), which does produce that order when run, instead of the then-runs-immediately thought that yields the correct answer.

findings.message: The feedback for '2 true' names the belief 'each new name for rota runs the module body again'. Worked through the code, the body already ran once on lines 2 to 5 (runs is 1), and the belief adds one more run for kitchen and one for bar, so runs would be 3, not 2. The named thought does not produce this option's value.
findings.resolution: Fixed: running a body once per user gives '2 false', so the option text was changed to '2 false' and its feedback now names the thought that each part runs the body (runs 2, separate objects), which the belief script confirmed.

findings.message: Option '250\n['ml']' feedback says the learner thought ml is listed because flags left out of the descriptor are true. Worked through, that belief also makes writable true, so cup.ml = 300 would succeed and the first line would print 300, not 250. The named belief does not give this option's value; the option really encodes 'read-only but still listed'.
findings.resolution: Fixed: the option now reads 300 and ['ml'] for the flags-default-true belief, the other wrong option 300 and [] is retagged to a new declared misconception (assignment always overwrites), and the feedback of both matches their values.

findings.message: The answer depends on typeof binding tighter than +, so that typeof price + ": " + price reads as (typeof price) + ": " + price; a wrong solution tests exactly this. Only the explanation states the rule. The lesson's card and the unit's earlier precedence rule (* and / before + and -) never say where typeof ranks against +, and the README says an explanation is not where a rule is taught.
findings.resolution: Fixed: the typeof concept card now says typeof is worked out before +, so the item's rule is taught on the card.
